tour.overview:
Saigon, officially Ho Chi Minh City since 1976, grew from a Khmer fishing village into the capital of French Cochinchina and then of South Vietnam. It is Vietnam's largest and most energetic city, of boulevards laid out by the French, colonial landmarks, glass towers and eight million motorbikes. Forty kilometres north-west, the villagers and fighters of Cu Chi dug a network of tunnels, some 250 kilometres long, that played a central role in the war against France and then the United States.

This private day explains the city's history with a licensed guide and a car. You visit the Cu Chi tunnels in the morning, have lunch, then see the Independence Palace, the War Remnants Museum and the colonial heart of the city, ending at Ben Thanh market and a rooftop bar at sunset.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Ho Chi Minh City
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; crawling in the tunnels is optional

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Cu Chi tunnels at Ben Dinh.
• The Independence Palace.
• The War Remnants Museum.
• Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Central Post Office.
• Ben Thanh market.

WHY THIS WORKS
We drive to Cu Chi early, before the heat and the big groups, and return to the city for the museums in the air-conditioned afternoon hours.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, veterans and their families, and first-time visitors to Saigon.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer rivers and rural life, choose our Mekong Delta day.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The tunnels are narrow, hot and dark even in the widened section; it is fine to stay above ground. The War Remnants Museum contains disturbing images, including of the effects of Agent Orange. Notre-Dame Cathedral is under long restoration; you see the façade.

days.name: The Cu Chi tunnels, a pho lunch, the Independence Palace, the War Remnants Museum, the colonial district and Ben Thanh market
days.description:
What to expect: the history of Saigon and the war, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:30 and drive north-west, about an hour and a half, to the Cu Chi tunnels at Ben Dinh. In the shade of a rubber and bamboo forest, you see how the network, begun against the French in the 1940s and extended in the 1960s, linked villages, command posts, hospitals and kitchens on three levels, with hidden entrances barely large enough for a small person, air vents disguised as termite mounds and smokeless kitchens. Your guide shows you the traps and explains daily life underground. If you wish, you can crawl through a section of about 30 to 100 metres, widened for visitors but still low, dark and hot.

Back in the city, you have lunch of pho, the beef noodle soup that is Vietnam's national dish. You then visit the Independence Palace, the presidential palace of South Vietnam, preserved as it was on 30 April 1975, when a North Vietnamese tank crashed through its gates and ended the war; you see the cabinet rooms, the presidential office and the bunker with its old radios and maps. At the War Remnants Museum, you see American aircraft and tanks in the courtyard, the photographs of war correspondents, and the galleries on the effects of Agent Orange, a sobering visit.

You walk through the colonial district: the red-brick Notre-Dame Cathedral, built with bricks shipped from Marseille between 1863 and 1880; the Central Post Office, with its iron vault and painted maps of the 1890s; and the Opera House on Dong Khoi street. You end at Ben Thanh market, under its clock tower, and watch the sunset over the city from a rooftop bar. Your driver takes you back to your hotel at about 18:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:00 – Cu Chi tunnels (about 2 hours).
12:30 – Pho lunch.
13:45 – Independence Palace.
15:00 – War Remnants Museum.
16:15 – Notre-Dame Cathedral, Central Post Office and Dong Khoi.
17:15 – Ben Thanh market and a rooftop view.
18:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The War Remnants Museum closes for lunch from 12:00 to 13:30; we plan around it.
• A speedboat to Cu Chi along the Saigon River can replace the drive.
• A street-food evening by scooter with experienced drivers can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, entrance tickets, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: shooting range at Cu Chi, rooftop drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we have to go into the tunnels?
faq.answer: No. Crawling through the tunnel section is optional; you can see the entrances, rooms and traps from above ground.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Cu Chi tunnels, the Independence Palace and the War Remnants Museum.

faq.question: Is the War Remnants Museum suitable for children?
faq.answer: Some galleries show very disturbing images. Your guide can choose a route for families or skip the museum.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, pho or another Vietnamese dish. Vegetarian versions are available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The city sites are accessible; Cu Chi has forest paths, and the tunnels themselves are not suitable.

faq.question: Can we go to Cu Chi by boat?
faq.answer: Yes, by speedboat on the Saigon River, as an option instead of the drive.

faq.question: Is there a shooting range at Cu Chi?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is not part of our tour, and we do not recommend it.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops at lacquer workshops unless you ask.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Vietnam but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes you don't mind getting dusty, comfortable shoes, a hat and insect repellent.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: December to April is dry. From May to November short, heavy afternoon showers are common.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
